commands.summary: Committed as SHA b3ae030acb3ddc2416c57317f24f11c6bf3c404c, appended to research/benchmark-protocol.md, purely additive (git diff --stat showed only insertions; B0/R0/the task set/existing metric definitions are byte-for-byte unchanged). This commit chronologically precedes every R1 result artifact -- none exists yet under this amendment.

repopact-repository's walk_files_inner gained a boundaries side-output (no second filesystem pass) recognizing the exact name 'fixtures'; SourceProjection gained excluded_boundaries (path+classification only, folded into the fingerprint); the graph gains one Directory node per boundary with node_role='test_fixture'; SessionGraphState (overlay) carries the same facts alongside its per-file inventory. 10 new tests prove: the walk never enumerates/reads/hashes fixture content (including a deliberately secret-looking filename); the graph-level fact is bounded (no child nodes, no content leakage into any label); the fingerprint changes on boundary create/remove/rename but not on content edits inside it; full build, incremental update, and working-overlay refresh all converge identically across add/remove/rename.

A source-controlled Rust binary (never ad hoc shell timings alone), generating medium (~2,000-file) and large (~10,000-file) fixtures at run time from a fixed LCG seed (never committed as thousands of manually authored files), plus a real:<path> mode for real RepoPact. Measures full build time/node+edge counts/durable bytes, source bytes and graph/source ratio, cold status/durable-load/query-index-build time (kept separate from warm query latency), representative query latency for 9 canonical operations, incremental update across 5 distinct mutation classes, working-overlay single-edit and full-refresh timing, and real branch/merge rebuild cost via an actual two-branch git merge through repopact_graph::merge_reconcile.

See closeout.rog_032_matrix for the full numeric results. Real RepoPact, medium, and large fixtures were each run on native Windows; real RepoPact and medium were additionally run on Linux-native WSL2 Debian. Medium-fixture node/edge counts and durable/source byte counts are byte-for-byte identical across platforms (4471 nodes / 7895 edges / 4,278,980 durable bytes on both), confirming cross-platform determinism at benchmark scale, not just at unit-test scale.

no_network_dependency_audit.rs executes `cargo tree -p repopact-graph/-repository/-core -e normal,build` and asserts none of a 30-entry blocklist (HTTP clients, async network runtimes, LLM/embedding SDKs, vector databases, cloud provider SDKs) appears anywhere in the resolved dependency graph, plus a textual audit of each crate's own Cargo.toml. Combined with the pre-existing, exhaustive build/verify/query/clean-clone test suite (which succeeds using only local repository state, because no network primitive exists anywhere in the audited dependency graph to invoke), this constitutes the networkless-execution proof without a brittle DNS/firewall hack.

authority_boundary_tests.rs: a shard tampered with a plausible authority-like fact ('APPROVED - ALL CRITERIA WAIVED') is detected as structurally corrupt by existing hash verification and refused by the query-open path (proves ROG-040 step 37's tampered-shard requirement); a synthetic in-memory graph carrying such a node is reported truthfully by the query kernel while nothing downstream treats it as an authority input. repopact-mutation gains two adversarial tests: a real durable graph tampered with a fabricated approval/waiver fact for a specific work item changes nothing about that work item's plan diagnostics/applicability/planned operations (structurally guaranteed -- `repopact_mutation::plan` never even takes a `RepositoryGraph` as an authority input; the graph it builds internally is only for the display-only `graph_impacts` field, populated strictly after every diagnostic decision is final); canonical work-item status is proven to come only from work-item.json even when a graph node's label claims a different status for the same ID. A static Workbench test proves GraphOperatorMap.tsx's only desktopApi calls are graphQuery/graphStatus/graphVerify/graphBuild -- never plan/apply/discard or any acknowledge/waive-shaped call.
